observations.explanation: The environment supports configured initial states, interactive keyboard/mouse actions, and execution-based evaluation; post-processing and retrieval before evaluation are described on PDF pp. 3–5. The claim’s characterization as enabling tasks beyond static action prediction is also consistent with the contrast on pp. 2, 8.

The paper reports 369 Ubuntu tasks and 43 Windows tasks, 134 evaluation functions, and task diversity including single-app, multi-app, and infeasible cases (PDF pp. 7–8). The broader assessment’s custom-evaluation characterization is supported by the example-specific scripts detailed on pp. 4–5, 7.
Table 5 reports GPT-4 at 12.24% overall and human performance at 72.36%; the table values and discussion support a substantial gap (PDF pp. 10–11).

The authors explicitly state that more time and further red-teaming could reduce false positives and negatives, leaving this for future work (PDF p. 8). The claim carefully frames this as a stated risk rather than proof that results are invalid.
